hypothesis: Longer spectral-difference spacing and logarithmic-frequency trajectory suppression can reduce false peaks without sacrificing real-onset recall or coverage.

mainMethods.full: Frozen production adjacent-frame full-band spectral flux; top2/DP actual cross-fit phase
mainMethods.lag5: Same linear-frequency log magnitude and full-band positive flux as full, but compare five frames apart
mainMethods.superflux: 24 bands/octave triangular logarithmic-frequency filterbank, log10(1+filtered magnitude), previous-frame maximum over three adjacent bands, five-frame difference

normalization: Frozen v557: subtract 0.7 times trailing 1000 ms mean, rectify at zero, divide by song maximum
peakPicking: Frozen v557: normalized threshold 0.02, 5 ms suppression radius, parabolic interpolation, bias 3*WIN/4/sampleRate
candidateMatching: Nearest peak within +/-10 ms around reference + frozen globalDelay + frozen actual cross-fit top2/DP phase; global controls use phase zero
weightRule: Frozen v557 stratum population / actually sampled objects
testPolicy: Do not retune parameters on these results. Any changed configuration requires a new version and a later independent confirmation set.
